original_value: Due to the ever-growing concerns over air pollution and energy security, more and more cities have started to replace their conventional taxi fleets with electric ones. Even though environmentally friendly, the rapid promotion of electric taxis raises problems to both taxi drivers and governments, e.g., prolonged waiting/charging time, unbalanced utilization of charging infrastructures, and inadequate taxi supply due to the long charging time. In this article, we conduct the first longitudinal measurement study to understand the long-term evolution of mobility and charging patterns by utilizing 5-year data from one of the largest electric taxi networks in the world, i.e., the Shenzhen electric taxi network in China. In particular, (1) we first perform an electric taxi contextualization about their operation and charging activities; (2) then we design a generic charging event extraction algorithm based on GPS data and charging station data, and (3) based on the contextualization and extracted charging activities, we perform a comprehensive measurement study called ePat to explore the evolution of the electric taxi network from the mobility and charging perspectives. Our ePat is based on 4.8 TB taxi GPS data, 240 GB taxi transaction data, and metadata from 117 charging stations, during an evolution process from 427 electric taxis in 2013 to 13,178 in 2018. Moreover, ePat also explores the impacts of various contexts and benefits during the evolution process. Our ePat as a comprehensive measurement of the electric taxi network mobility and charging evolution has the potential to advance the understanding of the evolution patterns of electric taxi networks and pave the way for analyzing future shared autonomous vehicles.

result.paraphrase: Rising air-pollution and energy-security concerns have led more cities to replace conventional taxi fleets with electric ones. Although greener, the rapid rollout of electric taxis creates challenges for drivers and governments, including longer waiting and charging times, uneven use of charging infrastructure, and insufficient taxi availability because charging takes so long. In this paper, we present the first longitudinal measurement study of long-term mobility and charging-pattern evolution using five years of data from one of the world’s largest electric taxi networks, the Shenzhen electric taxi network in China. Specifically, we first contextualize electric taxi operations and charging behavior; next, we develop a generic charging-event extraction algorithm using GPS data and charging-station data; and finally, based on the contextualization and extracted charging activities, we conduct a comprehensive measurement study, ePat, to examine the network’s evolution from both mobility and charging perspectives. ePat relies on 4.8 TB of taxi GPS data, 240 GB of taxi transaction data, and metadata from 117 charging stations, spanning the network’s growth from 427 electric taxis in 2013 to 13,178 in 2018. It also investigates how various contexts and benefits affect this evolution. As a comprehensive measurement of mobility and charging evolution in an electric taxi network, ePat can deepen understanding of evolution patterns in electric taxi networks and help prepare for future analyses of shared autonomous vehicles.
